summary: Cameron Bailey works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University, Florida State University, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), where his supervisors and teachers included Bryan J. Cuevas, Richard F. Nance, and Ulrike Roesler.

Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Harvard University, studying under Yudru Tsomu. He has held academic posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.
Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Attested in 2018, he earned his MA at Florida State University under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas.

Camillo Alessio Formigatti specializes in Indology and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Milan, he worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at Cambridge (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS, and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Library (attested 2019).

Carel Gabriel Cobet (1813–1889) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. After attending Gymnasium Haganum and studying at Leiden University (~1832–1836), he held posts at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.

Carl A. P. Ruck (born 1935) works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1956–1959) and Harvard University (~1961–1965), and held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, earning his PhD at UC Berkeley in 1980. He held an editorial board post at Stanford University (~1980–2017).

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber at Berlin, and also at Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD ~1868), and Jena (Habilitation 1872), where he became professor in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn (1795–1864) was a Danish scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from around 1814 to 1816 and held a post there around 1826.

Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was an American linguist. He studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and Leipzig University (~1889–1892), and served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

Carl Gaedicke is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Jena, completing his PhD by 1877 under the instruction of Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) studied medicine at the University of Basel (1895–1900). A scholar of psychology and religious studies, he held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1914), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

Carl Olson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College, attested between 2005 and 2015.

Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig University under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Humboldt University of Berlin. In 1847 he became Lektor and in 1857 professor at the University of Oslo.

Carl Schuster (1904–1969) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University from around 1926 to 1930 and at the University of Vienna from around 1930 to 1934.
Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber, Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, and Rudolf von Roth at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Tübingen, later holding posts at Trinity College Dublin, Schulpforta, and Jena (~1875–1903).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Stanford (AB ~1973) and Harvard (PhD ~1981), taught at Pomona College (1981–1992), and served as professor at UNC Chapel Hill from 1992 to 2022.

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a linguist and historian. After studies in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he held posts at the École française d'Athènes, the University of Groningen (1903; 1908–1916), and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Italian Indologist. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Georg Bühler, Hermann Oldenberg, and Paul Deussen (Kiel University). He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).
